overpriced - This is a polyphosphate cartridge. Practically, it cannot "filter" the scale-causing minerals from the water, as there is far too much volume of minerals to hold in the tiny cartridge. Instead, the cartridge releases a small amount of polyphosphates into the water. Those chemicals inhibit the formation of the scale -- in simple terms, they keep the minerals suspended in the water and inhibit them from forming the white deposits. Of course, the minerals have to go somewhere, and they can't stay suspended indefinitely as they won't evaporate as steam. Some of the mineral material inevitably forms scale, while the rest is flushed out of the humidifier tank in the flush cycle (which is frequently problematic on the troublesome TrueSteam humidifiers). So the polyphosphates released by this cartridge help to inhibit scale by keeping the minerals suspended until they get flushed.

Now that you understand how it works, you can go get a standard 1/4" quick-connect, in-line polyphosphate scale-inhibiting filter that's twice the size for half the price. Either way, you can only expect it to last about 6 months. The polyphosphates used in these filters are "food grade" and considered acceptable for whole-house use, including drinking water (although there's no benefit for drinking). Polyphosphates are sometimes used in lieu of water softeners.

Simple Solution For Washer Ventilation - These door stand-off devices are a no-brainer solution to the problem of washer laundry appliances developing mildew smells and helps slow the build-up of mold in the rubber door seals.

To use them it is required your appliance(s) have metal on the face so that the magnet can be attracted for stabilizing the stand-off. In my case the two washers we have a Whirlpool brand, model WFW92HEFUO, that have a stainless steel finish but the magnets still grab on and do their job. Granted this review is being written immediately after installing the two units I bought. The magnetic strength is not especially strong but the magnets in the two units I received definitely have enough power to hold themselves in place and do their intended job. Please note, if your appliance(s) have a stainless steel finish there's a possibility these might not work since not all stainless steels are magnetic.

It's also nice there is a rubber coating on the magnet surface itself which not only prevents it from scratching your appliance but it also gives a bit of a tack to the device which helps prevent it from sliding down from the place you choose to mount it.

Overall these are a very simple solution to a very common problem of mal odor from front-loader laundry washing machines.
